listing.name: Wario Land 4 (BioRhythmic Studios)
listing.summary: An unofficial native PC port of Wario Land 4. The upstream launcher needs your own unmodified US Game Boy Advance ROM.

steps.title: Open the upstream Windows launcher
steps.instruction: On Windows, select the Windows x64 release, extract the entire ZIP into a folder you own, and open wl4-launcher.exe. Keep both EXEs, SDL3.dll, and the notices together.

steps.title: Select the Linux AppImage
steps.instruction: Use the official Linux x64 AppImage on a host with glibc 2.38 or later. Make the file executable. In Portcove, select the AppImage and use its containing folder as the working directory. If FUSE is unavailable, enter --appimage-extract-and-run as one argument.

steps.title: Choose your original game
steps.instruction: In the launcher, choose Browse and select your own unmodified US Game Boy Advance ROM. The launcher checks for an 8 MiB file with game code AWAE and MD5 5fe47355a33e3fabec2a1607af88a404. Choose Launch Game.

warnings: The packages contain recompiled game program code. Upstream's MIT notice covers its identified sources, and upstream documents inherited code with no recorded license. The launcher reads game data from your own original ROM.

The Windows v0.3.2-beta runtime could not start on the Windows 11 build 26300 host tested by Portcove. This release could not reserve the memory range it needs for the game. See upstream for newer beta releases.

The Windows launcher saves the selected ROM path in your user registry. Windows v0.3.2-beta can read earlier settings, but beta 1 and beta 2 cannot read the newer settings it saves. Back up settings before downgrading.

data_locations: the Windows user registry entry for the original ROM path

presentation.manual_preparation: Download the official Linux x64 AppImage and mark it executable. Add the AppImage to Portcove with its containing folder. Use --appimage-extract-and-run as an argument if FUSE is unavailable. In the upstream launcher, choose your own unmodified US Game Boy Advance ROM. Portcove leaves the AppImage, the ROM and your XDG save and settings folders in place. Use upstream’s releases to replace the AppImage yourself.
